3.shows: Earth seen from the International Space Station in orbit (station hardware may be in frame)
3.line: Distance was never the problem. The station circles Earth about every ninety minutes, moving at roughly seventeen thousand five hundred miles an hour.

5.shows: Earth turning beneath the International Space Station as it flies its path (no launch footage: NASA shuttle/launch clips failed QA)
5.line: And there's essentially one shot a day, the brief moment when Earth's spin carries the launch pad right under the station's orbital path.
